title: Calculate Monthly Revenue
description: Write a query that returns revenue grouped by calendar month, as `month` and `revenue`, ordered chronologically (earliest month first). Use `DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)` to collapse every order_date onto the first day of its month.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DATE_TRUNC, GROUP BY on a date expression
DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) turns e.g. 2025-03-15 into 2025-03-01 - group by that EXPRESSION (not the raw order_date) so every day in the same month collapses into one row.

SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id, grouped by DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date), ordered by month.
expected_behavior: Returns one row per calendar month that had any orders, with total revenue for that month, oldest month first.
solution: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) ORDER BY month;
explanation: DATE_TRUNC is the standard PostgreSQL way to bucket timestamps/dates into coarser periods (month, week, year, ...) - grouping by the raw order_date would give one row per DAY instead of per month, which isn't what a monthly trend report needs.
postgres_note: DATE_TRUNC is PostgreSQL-specific syntax - other databases spell this differently (MySQL has no direct equivalent and typically uses DATE_FORMAT instead).
